stem: Which choice states what follows when you link both facts?
stimulus:
Fact 1: Every impression printed from Ilse Varga's copper plates in 1890 carries a faint diagonal scratch near its lower margin.
Fact 2: The impression owned by the Hartwell Library was printed from Varga's copper plates in 1890.
Taken together, these facts show that the Hartwell impression ______
choices: carries a faint diagonal scratch near its lower margin.
was printed from Varga's copper plates in 1890.
is the only Varga impression that carries the scratch.
was printed earlier than Varga's other impressions.
explanation: The shared term is 'printed from Varga's plates in 1890.' Fact 1 says everything in that group has the scratch. Fact 2 puts the Hartwell impression in that group. If you remove the shared term, you get Hartwell impression → scratch. This is the move behind the 'link the two facts' inference questions: no single sentence gives you the answer, and you only reach it by connecting the facts.

B.why: You picked a choice that repeats Fact 2. It is true, but it uses only half the evidence. The question asks what you learn by combining both facts, and this choice tells you nothing new.

C.why: Fact 1 says every 1890 impression has the scratch, so the Hartwell copy can't be the only one. You let 'only' slip past you. Circle quantifiers like that before you choose.

D.why: Neither fact compares dates across Varga's impressions. You added a step that the passage never establishes.

stem: Which choice states what follows when you link both facts?
stimulus:
Fact 1: All of the pottery found in the lowest layer at the Tel Marun site was made with crushed shell mixed into the clay.
Fact 2: In this region, shell-tempered pottery was made only by communities living near the coast.
Taken together, these facts show that the pottery in the lowest layer ______
choices: was made with crushed shell mixed into the clay.
was made by communities living near the coast.
was made at the site when it lay near the coast.
was the only pottery those coastal communities made.
explanation: The shared term is 'shell-tempered' pottery. Fact 1 says the lowest-layer pottery is shell-tempered. Fact 2 says only coastal communities made shell-tempered pottery. If you remove the shared term, you get lowest-layer pottery → made by coastal communities. On real inference questions, the answer is often this small, plain link and nothing more.

A.why: This repeats Fact 1 and never uses Fact 2. A choice that restates one premise has not linked anything, and it is the most common trap on this subtype.

C.why: This is the extra-step trap. The facts tell you who made the pottery, not where it was made. Coastal communities could have made it elsewhere and traded it inland. You assumed something the passage doesn't state.

D.why: Nothing says what other pottery the coastal communities made. The word 'only' takes the claim past what the two facts establish.

stem: Which choice states what follows when you link both facts?
stimulus:
Fact 1: In a study of songbirds, every species that fed mainly on insects left its breeding grounds before September.
Fact 2: None of the species that left their breeding grounds before September were recorded at the study's feeders in October.
Taken together, these facts show that the insect-eating species in the study ______
choices: left their breeding grounds before September.
were not recorded at the feeders in October.
were replaced at the feeders by seed eaters.
were the only species to leave before September.
explanation: The shared term is 'left before September.' Fact 1 says the insect eaters all left before September. Fact 2 says no species that left before September showed up at the feeders in October. If you remove the shared term, you get insect eaters → not at the feeders in October. Chains like this, including negative ones, are the core of the 'link the two facts' inference questions.

A.why: This repeats Fact 1. It is true, but it ignores Fact 2, so it is not the conclusion the two facts produce together.

C.why: The passage never says what was at the feeders in October. Saying seed eaters took the insect eaters' place adds a new claim that neither fact supports.

D.why: You reversed Fact 1. It says all insect eaters left early. It does not say that only insect eaters left early, so other species may have left early too.

stem: Which choice states what follows when you link both facts?
stimulus:
Fact 1: Fog forms at the Carrow Valley airport only when the overnight air there cools to its dew point.
Fact 2: On nights with heavy cloud cover, the overnight air at the Carrow Valley airport never cools to its dew point.
Taken together, these facts show that on heavily clouded nights at the airport, ______
choices: the overnight air does not cool to its dew point.
fog forms only after the cloud cover has cleared.
fog forms more slowly than it does on clear nights.
fog does not form at the airport during the night.
explanation: The shared term is 'cools to its dew point.' Fact 1 says fog requires that cooling. Fact 2 says that cooling never happens on cloudy nights. If you remove the shared term, you get cloudy night → no fog. This is the chain you build on real inference questions that end with 'taken together' or 'therefore.'

A.why: This repeats Fact 2. It is true, but it never reaches fog, which is what linking Fact 1 adds.

B.why: The facts say what happens when clouds are present, not what happens after they clear. Even on clear nights, the air might not reach its dew point. You added a step.

C.why: The facts rule out fog completely on cloudy nights, so it doesn't form slowly. It doesn't form at all. The comparison to clear nights also goes beyond anything the passage establishes.
